newsitem.title: UK: German contract for millennium dome riles UK press.
newsitem.headline: German contract for millennium dome riles UK press.

text.p: Xenophobic British media and politicians voiced outrage on Monday at news that a German company had won a contract for the centrepiece of a lavish London development to celebrate the new millennium.

But government officials dismissed the row, saying the British construction industry had won the lion's share of the work to build a "Millennium Dome" at Greenwich, east London. The Greenwich meridian is used as an international basis of time-reckoning.

The right-wing Daily Mail headlined its report that Munich's Koch Konstruktive Membrane company had a 6.1-million-pound ($9.8 million) contract on the near 20-acre (eight-hectare) dome "Made in Germany. Can't anyone in Britain build our...dome?"

Conservative member of parliament Sir Teddy Taylor, a prominent anti-European, said: "It is appalling that this great white elephant which is designed to display British achievements at the millennium should have a German dome on top of it."

But an official in Prime Minister Tony Blair's office said the role to be played by foreign construction firms in building the 250-million-pound exhibition centre, a favourite project of the Labour government, had been exaggerated by the headlines.

He said some 25 of the 30 contracts had already been awarded, and all but one had gone to British firms. The one exception, which had gone to Koch Konstruktive, was for the fabric which will cover the circular dome.
"We are not talking about the mushroom itself. We are talking about the skin of the mushroom," the official said.

He pointed out that all government construction contracts worth over 150,000 pounds have to be advertised in a European Union official journal, and bids from any of the 15 member states must be considered.
